title: Pardes Rimonim (Orchard of Pomegranates)
author: Moses Cordovero (Sefaria Community trans)
description: Pardes Rimonim (Orchard of Pomegranates) by Rabbi Moses Cordovero (the Ramak, 1522-1570), the leading Kabbalist of Safed before Isaac Luria, here in the community English translation from Sefaria. Completed around 1548 and divided into thirty-two 'gates', it is the first comprehensive systematisation of Kabbalah, reconciling the diverse views in the Zohar and earlier Kabbalists. Cordovero discusses the Ein Sof and its relation to the sefirot, whether the sefirot are God's essence or vessels, their order, emanation and names, the divine names and their combinations, the channels connecting the sefirot, the worlds, the soul, the 'shells' (kelippot), and the mysteries of letters, vowels and prayer. Its rigorous, philosophical approach made it the classic textbook of pre-Lurianic Kabbalah.
